name: Card network product owner
goals: Define the agentic token format and lifecycle that issuers, acquirers and agent providers implement.
Run an agent registration and key directory so merchants and CDNs can recognize trusted agents.
Publish rules for agent transactions: indicators, step-up, disputes and liability.
Grow acceptance through PSPs, CDNs and agent platforms without forcing merchants to rebuild checkout.
Keep card rails relevant against stablecoin pay-per-call protocols by joining their governance (the x402 Foundation, the MPP card method).
Align with IETF Web Bot Auth, FIDO and EMVCo so the network scheme does not become a proprietary island.
pains: The network's own spec (TAP) sits under revocable proprietary terms and lags the IETF draft, which draws criticism.
Agent indicators are not populated reliably, so fraud models and issuers cannot rely on them.
Live agent transactions are still controlled pilots, and no public volume exists to show progress.

Visa's rules make the cardholder responsible, within Visa's system, for an Agentic Payment Provider's actions. Neither Visa nor Mastercard has published agent-specific dispute reason codes, Worldpay says no liability shift exists yet, and every issuer and acquirer is asking.
Agents filling checkout forms with token-shaped values keep legacy acceptance alive but defeat the purpose of agent recognition.
Two networks run two different directories and two different token definitions, and merchants want one.
decisions: Token scoping model: per interaction, per merchant, or per mandate.
Rules for liability and dispute reason codes on agent-initiated transactions.
Which identity protocols to accept (own directory, Web Bot Auth, Know Your Agent partners).
Which external standards bodies to align with and when to retire the proprietary spec.
Program requirements for agent certification and trusted lists.
